c1: Baseline: parallel Hash Join reading all of chartevents (2 workers), then filtering ~3.8k qualifying rows by the charttime join filter. Almost all work is scanning rows that are discarded. Optimized: Nested Loop over 140 stays, each doing an Index Only Scan on (itemid, stay_id, charttime) INCLUDE (valuenum), so only matching index entries are read and the heap is never visited.
c2: Baseline: SubPlan 1 executes once per outer row (loops = 11,814). Each loop builds a BitmapAnd of two indexes, fetches about 44 heap rows and runs a top-N heapsort. Optimized: a single Bitmap Heap Scan, one in-memory quicksort (about 1 MB) and a WindowAgg. The per-row repeated work disappears.
c3: Baseline: Seq Scan of all 107,727 lab events, Hash Join to d_labitems, then a full Sort (about 8.9 MB in memory) to evaluate COUNT(DISTINCT hadm_id) per group. Optimized: Seq Scan of 498 pre-aggregated rows. The cost moves to view creation and refresh (see setup cost); the view pays off only when it is read more than once per refresh.
c4: Baseline: five SubPlans, each a full Seq Scan of chartevents executed once per ICU stay (loops = 140), removing about 668,800 rows per scan. That is 700 full scans of the table. Optimized: one Seq Scan with the itemid IN-list filter, a Hash Right Join to icustays and one HashAggregate.
c5: Baseline: COUNT(DISTINCT) forces a GroupAggregate fed by a full Sort of 668,862 rows on (itemid, stay_id) using about 45 MB of memory. Optimized: two HashAggregates (first de-duplicating to 40,587 pairs, then counting), with no sort. The gain is real but modest (about 2-3x) because both plans still scan the whole table.
